REQUIRED_ACCEPTANCE_EVIDENCE_FLOOR.status: BINDING. This is the complete required minimum. Nothing outside it may be enforced as a requirement by this authority.
elements: instrument identity — the instrument_key the acceptance is against
version — which published edition of that instrument was accepted
content digest — the cryptographic identity of the accepted bytes, with the algorithm recorded alongside it

the accepting subject or actor, WHERE STRUCTURALLY REQUIRED BY THE ACCEPTANCE ACT — the subject for an account-class acceptance, and the organization plus the acting organization_admin for an organization-class acceptance
REQUIRED_ACCEPTANCE_EVIDENCE_FLOOR.canonical_basis: HPO-A.4 names the first four. The fifth is ENTAILED by HPO-A.1 and HPO-A.3, which fix a different accepting principal for each instrument class; an acceptance that recorded no actor could not satisfy either clause. See HPO_A_PROVENANCE_R2.DRIFT_COMPARISON.DELTA_1A_SUBJECT.
EXPLICITLY_OUTSIDE_THE_FLOOR: Durable retention of instrument bytes or an immutable content reference — RECOMMENDED_NOT_REQUIRED, see INSTRUMENT_MODEL.INSTRUMENT_IDENTITY_TUPLE.content_identity.CONTENT_RETENTION_SHAPE.
Any identifying metadata beyond the actor identity — no IP address, user agent, device or fingerprint is required, and none may be added without LRF-03 answered. Unchanged from R1.
Any notice, acknowledgement or display record. Notice is permitted and is not acceptance.
REQUIRED_ACCEPTANCE_EVIDENCE_FLOOR.conformance_consequence: A control, gate, invariant or review checklist derived from this authority MUST be satisfiable by an implementation holding exactly the floor above and nothing else.

REACCEPTANCE.governing_decision: HPO-A decision 5 - reaccept only when a later instrument version is explicitly marked reaccept_required.

THE_CURRENCY_PREDICATE.informal: A subject or organization is CURRENT on instrument_key K if they have accepted some version V of K, and no version of K later than V is marked reaccept_required.
THE_CURRENCY_PREDICATE.formal: current(P, K) := EXISTS v_a in accepted(P, K) such that NOT EXISTS v_r in published(K) with v_r > v_a AND v_r.reaccept_required = true. Where more than one version has been accepted, v_a is the greatest.

WHAT_THIS_PREDICATE_IS_NOT.not_latest_version_equality: current is NOT accepted_version == latest_version. That form ignores decision 5 entirely and would force reacceptance on every publication, including typo corrections.
WHAT_THIS_PREDICATE_IS_NOT.not_latest_reaccept_required_version: current is NOT accepted_version >= greatest version marked reaccept_required, as a standalone test - because that form returns TRUE for a subject who has accepted NOTHING when no version has ever been marked reaccept_required. The EXISTS clause on an actual acceptance is load-bearing and must not be optimised away.
WHAT_THIS_PREDICATE_IS_NOT.why_that_second_error_is_the_dangerous_o: It is invisible in every ordinary test. With one instrument version, never marked reaccept_required, a subject who has accepted nothing passes. The gate would appear to work in staging - where no reacceptance has ever been published - and would be wide open. A negative control must therefore assert refusal for a subject with ZERO acceptances specifically, and not only for a subject with a stale one.

worked_examples.published: v1, v2, v3; none marked reaccept_required

worked_examples.why: no marked version later than v2
the EXISTS clause fails - this is the case the second wrong form gets wrong

PRIOR_ACCEPTANCES_ARE_NEVER_DELETED_OR_I.ruling: When reacceptance becomes required, the prior acceptance row is untouched. Currency is a computed property of the row set plus the version set; it is never a column on the acceptance.
PRIOR_ACCEPTANCES_ARE_NEVER_DELETED_OR_I.why_a_stored_is_current_column_is_forbid: It would have to be UPDATEd on every publication of a marked version - across every subject in the system - which contradicts APPEND_ONLY, makes the most safety-critical value in the model a cached one, and creates a partial-failure state in which some subjects are correctly marked stale and others are not. Computing the predicate has a read cost; storing it has a correctness cost.

MULTI_INSTRUMENT_CONJUNCTION.ruling: L0 passes only if the subject is current on EVERY published account-class instrument_key. L1 passes only if the organization is current on EVERY published organization-class instrument_key.
MULTI_INSTRUMENT_CONJUNCTION.fail_closed_shape: The gate is a conjunction over the CLOSED SET of published keys for the class, evaluated against the live registry - never against a hardcoded list of keys in application code. A hardcoded list silently stops gating any instrument added later.
MULTI_INSTRUMENT_CONJUNCTION.control: M-AO-4 asserts that adding a published account-class instrument that the subject has not accepted turns L0 refusing, without any application code change.

THE_REACCEPTANCE_JOURNEY_POSITION.ruling: Reacceptance is enforced at the SAME gate and the SAME position as first acceptance. There is no separate reacceptance flow and no grace period.
THE_REACCEPTANCE_JOURNEY_POSITION.grounds: HPO-A decision 5 changes only WHEN the predicate goes false; it does not create a second gate. A subject who becomes non-current is refused exactly as a subject who never accepted, which keeps the topology at one gate per class.
THE_REACCEPTANCE_JOURNEY_POSITION.grace_period_disposition: NOT AUTHORIZED. HPO-A grants none, and a grace period is precisely a period during which the gate is open. If the owner wants one, it is new policy. Recorded as OPEN_FINDINGS.F-AO-08.
THE_REACCEPTANCE_JOURNEY_POSITION.the_operational_consequence_that_must_be: Publishing a version marked reaccept_required refuses EVERY affected subject or organization at their next request, immediately. For an account-class instrument that is the entire user base. This is the correct fail-closed behaviour and it is also an operational event of the highest severity - which is why PUBLICATION_IS_A_GOVERNED_ACT restricts who may cause it.

R2_CORRECTION_EFFECTIVE_AT.status: BINDING CORRECTION. R1 predicate is SUPERSEDED in one dimension and preserved in every other.
R2_CORRECTION_EFFECTIVE_AT.governing_ratification: RAT-AO-03, clauses AO3_C2, AO3_C3 and AO3_C4.

WHAT_R1_GOT_WRONG.the_R1_predicate: current(P,K) := EXISTS v_a in accepted(P,K) such that NOT EXISTS v_r in published(K) with v_r > v_a AND v_r.reaccept_required = true.
WHAT_R1_GOT_WRONG.the_defect: It has NO TIME DIMENSION. Publication alone makes a marked version bite. Under RAT-AO-03 that is WRONG: a version carrying reaccept_required true whose effective_at is in the FUTURE must NOT yet refuse, because AO3_C3 says the pre-effective period is for notice and the product is NOT REQUIRED to block on it.
WHAT_R1_GOT_WRONG.the_consequence_if_uncorrected: Publishing a future-dated instrument version would refuse the entire affected population IMMEDIATELY, on publication, weeks before the version takes effect. That is the exact false-lockout failure R1 warned about for a different wrong predicate, arriving through a door R1 had not modelled.
WHAT_R1_GOT_WRONG.R1_status: SUPERSEDED IN THIS DIMENSION ONLY. R1 text is retained above for auditability; this correction governs.

THE_CORRECTED_CURRENCY_PREDICATE.informal: A subject or organization is CURRENT on instrument_key K if they have accepted some version V of K, and no version of K that is later than V, marked reaccept_required, and already in effect has superseded it.
THE_CORRECTED_CURRENCY_PREDICATE.formal: current(P, K, t) := EXISTS v_a in accepted(P, K) such that NOT EXISTS v_r in published(K) with v_r > v_a AND v_r.reaccept_required = true AND effective(v_r, t). Where v_a is the greatest accepted version, and effective(v_r, t) := (v_r.effective_at IS NULL) OR (v_r.effective_at <= t).
the_three_conjuncts_that_must_ALL_hold_f: it is LATER than the accepted version
it is ALREADY IN EFFECT at evaluation time
THE_CORRECTED_CURRENCY_PREDICATE.DERIVED_NOT_GRANTED: Still a derivation — neither ratification states the NULL semantics in those words — but grounded at R3 in HPO-A.5 (the base transition rule) plus RAT-AO-03 AO3_C2 and AO3_C4 (effective_at as an OPTIONAL deferral of that rule), rather than in the eliminative two-readings argument R2 used. See EFFECTIVE_AT_NULL_GROUNDS_R3.
THE_CORRECTED_CURRENCY_PREDICATE.R2_REASONING_SUPERSEDED_AT_R3: AO3_C2 says a version MAY carry an effective_at — MAY, not MUST. A version without one is not invalid, so the predicate must handle its absence, and there are only two candidate readings. Treating NULL as NOT-YET-EFFECTIVE would mean a version published with reaccept_required true and no date NEVER bites, which converts an omitted optional field into a permanent silent bypass. Treating NULL as IN EFFECT ON PUBLICATION makes the omission mean the version takes effect immediately, which is the fail-closed reading and matches R1 behaviour for the case R1 modelled.

EFFECTIVE_AT_NULL_GROUNDS_R3.conclusion_PRESERVED: effective_at = NULL means the version is IN EFFECT ON PUBLICATION.
EFFECTIVE_AT_NULL_GROUNDS_R3.R2_REASONING_WITHDRAWN: R2 grounded this on the assertion that there are only two candidate readings, and then eliminated one. That is a false dichotomy: other readings are constructible — for example that a NULL-dated marked version is inert until a date is supplied, or that it takes effect at some derived time. Eliminating one alternative does not establish the remaining one, and the conclusion deserves positive grounds rather than an argument by exhaustion over a set that was never shown to be exhaustive.

THE_POSITIVE_GROUNDS.step_1_the_base_rule: HPO-A.5 states the base transition rule: reacceptance triggers on a governed reaccept_required version transition. The trigger is the TRANSITION itself. Nothing in HPO-A.5 conditions it on a date.
THE_POSITIVE_GROUNDS.step_2_the_optional_deferral: RAT-AO-03 AO3_C2 says each legal-instrument version MAY carry a governed effective_at — MAY, not MUST. AO3_C4 then says that FROM effective_at onward the marked version stops a prior acceptance satisfying the gate. So effective_at operates as an OPTIONAL DEFERRAL of a rule that HPO-A.5 already established.
THE_POSITIVE_GROUNDS.step_3_the_conclusion: Where the optional deferral is ABSENT, there is nothing to defer, and the base rule of HPO-A.5 applies unmodified: the transition triggers on publication. NULL is therefore not an ambiguity to be resolved by choosing between readings — it is the ABSENCE OF A MODIFIER to a rule that stands on its own.
THE_POSITIVE_GROUNDS.why_this_is_stronger_than_the_R2_argumen: It derives the answer from what the two ratifications say, in order, rather than from the unprovable claim that no third reading exists. It also explains WHY the answer is what it is: effective_at defers, and an absent deferral defers nothing.

EFFECTIVE_AT_NULL_GROUNDS_R3.the_fail_closed_property_is_a_consequenc: This reading also happens to be the fail-closed one, because the alternative would let an omitted optional field permanently suppress a marked transition. That is a welcome CONSEQUENCE and is recorded as such. It is no longer the load-bearing argument, which matters: a conclusion that rests only on being safe is a conclusion an auditor can challenge on grounds of authority, and this one now rests on authority.
EFFECTIVE_AT_NULL_GROUNDS_R3.DERIVED_NOT_GRANTED: Still labelled as a derivation, because neither ratification states the NULL semantics in those words. But the derivation is now from cited clauses (HPO-A.5 plus AO3_C2 and AO3_C4) rather than from an eliminative argument.
EFFECTIVE_AT_NULL_GROUNDS_R3.control: N-AO-32 and P-AO-19 are unchanged and continue to pin the behaviour; M-AO-18 continues to mutate to the inverted reading.

WHAT_IS_PRESERVED_FROM_R1_UNCHANGED.the_EXISTS_clause: THE FAIL-CLOSED PROPERTY IS PRESERVED VERBATIM AND IS NOT WEAKENED BY THE TIME DIMENSION. A subject with NO acceptance record must NEVER pass merely because no version currently has reaccept_required true, and must equally never pass merely because every marked version is not yet effective. The EXISTS clause over an ACTUAL acceptance is load-bearing and must not be optimised away. R1 named this the dangerous wrong form and that judgement stands unchanged.
WHAT_IS_PRESERVED_FROM_R1_UNCHANGED.why_the_new_dimension_makes_the_old_trap: Before the correction there was one way to reach a vacuous pass: no version marked. Now there are TWO: no version marked, OR every marked version still pre-effective. The second is MORE likely in practice, because a team publishing a future-dated version has deliberately created exactly that state. A subject with zero acceptances must be refused in BOTH, and a control that only exercises the first is incomplete.
WHAT_IS_PRESERVED_FROM_R1_UNCHANGED.no_stored_currency_flag: PRESERVED. I-X-1 and I-X-5 stand: no is_current, no is_valid, no denormalized acceptance boolean anywhere. The time dimension STRENGTHENS this — a cached flag would now have to be invalidated by the CLOCK, not merely by a publication event, which means no write-time hook could keep it correct.
WHAT_IS_PRESERVED_FROM_R1_UNCHANGED.append_only: PRESERVED. Reacceptance adds a row; prior acceptances are never deleted or invalidated in place.
WHAT_IS_PRESERVED_FROM_R1_UNCHANGED.multi_instrument_conjunction: PRESERVED. The gate is a conjunction over the live registry of published instruments for the class, never a hardcoded list.
WHAT_IS_PRESERVED_FROM_R1_UNCHANGED.same_gate_same_position: PRESERVED. Reacceptance is enforced at the same gate and position as first acceptance. There is no separate reacceptance flow.

GRACE_PERIOD_DISPOSITION_UPDATED.R1_said: NOT AUTHORIZED, recorded as F-AO-08 STOP_FOR_HPO awaiting an owner decision.
GRACE_PERIOD_DISPOSITION_UPDATED.R2_says: RESOLVED BY RATIFICATION. RAT-AO-03 AO3_C1: there is NO universal reacceptance grace period. F-AO-08 moves from STOP_FOR_HPO to RESOLVED_BY_RATIFICATION, and the R1 posture was correct.
GRACE_PERIOD_DISPOSITION_UPDATED.no_number_invented: No grace duration appears anywhere in this artifact. See RAT_AO_CONSUMPTION.RAT_AO_03.NO_GRACE_DURATION_IS_INVENTED for why effective_at is structurally not a grace period.

PRE_EFFECTIVE_NOTICE.status: PERMITTED, NOT REQUIRED, AND NOT A GATE.
PRE_EFFECTIVE_NOTICE.grounds: AO3_C3 — before effective_at the product MAY inform the user and is NOT REQUIRED to block on it.
binding_consequences: A pre-effective version MUST NOT refuse at L0 or L1.

Notice is NOT an acceptance. Displaying, dismissing or acknowledging a pre-effective notice creates NO acceptance row and does NOT pre-satisfy the future gate. An acceptance may only bind a version the subject actually accepted.

Accepting a pre-effective version, if the product offers that, IS a real acceptance of that version and counts once the version takes effect. The acceptance binds the version, not the moment the gate closes.
No notice copy, surface or timing is designed or required here. AO3_C5 keeps notice sufficiency and timing COUNSEL_REQUIRED.

ENFORCEMENT_TOPOLOGY.status: BINDING AS A SHAPE. The exact line anchors are RE-MEASUREMENT OBLIGATIONS, not pins, because Packet B must land first and will itself edit several of these sites.

THE_SHAPE_IS_CARRIED_FROM_PACKET_B_NOT_R.principle: ONE derivation, ONE propagation, N translations - where N is fixed by how many distinct refusal vocabularies the codebase already has, not by how many places the policy is restated.
THE_SHAPE_IS_CARRIED_FROM_PACKET_B_NOT_R.why_it_applies_unchanged_to_L0: L0 is the same kind of predicate as B0: a per-subject boolean, resolved once per request, consumed at boundaries that already have refusal vocabularies. Nothing about it argues for a different shape, and inventing one would leave two topologies to audit instead of one.

derivation_point.requirement: The account-acceptance currency fact is derived ONCE per request, on the principal-resolution path, and propagated onto the RequestPrincipal alongside the verification fact Packet B adds.
derivation_point.measured_seam: Packet B derives its fact at lib/auth/identity.ts:125 and propagates at lib/auth/database-context.ts:536 inside resolveRequestPrincipal, which it proves is the SOLE consumer of getVerifiedAuthIdentityResult() for the request-principal family. L0 attaches to the same propagation point.
derivation_point.THE_DIFFERENCE_FROM_B0_THAT_MUST_BE_STAT: B0 predicate comes from the auth provider and costs no query. L0 predicate requires reading the acceptance and version relations, so it adds a DATABASE READ to the principal path. That is a real cost and it is accepted, because the alternative - checking at each boundary - multiplies the read by the number of boundaries and reintroduces the duplication Packet B eliminated. The read must be ONE query, evaluated once, memoised with the principal.
derivation_point.consequence_for_the_read: The currency predicate is a conjunction over published account-class instruments (REACCEPTANCE.MULTI_INSTRUMENT_CONJUNCTION). It must be expressible as a single set-returning query, not a loop over instruments issued per request.

THE_MEMO_TRAP_IS_INHERITED.status: BINDING CONSTRAINT, carried verbatim in substance from Packet B R4.
THE_MEMO_TRAP_IS_INHERITED.measured_fact: requirePrincipal consults the memo FIRST - lib/auth/database-context.ts:632-633, const memoised = await loadRequestPrincipal(); if (memoised) return memoised - and returns from :633 WITHOUT reaching resolveRequestPrincipal at :635 or the throw at :639.
THE_MEMO_TRAP_IS_INHERITED.the_defect_this_forbids: An L0 check placed after :635, on the fresh-resolution branch, is BYPASSED whenever the memo is warm. The failure is INTERMITTENT - it depends on whether an earlier call in the same request already resolved the principal - which makes it the worst class of gate defect: it passes tests that happen to run cold and opens in production paths that run warm.
THE_MEMO_TRAP_IS_INHERITED.requirement: The L0 translation at C6 MUST bind the RESULT of principal resolution, on both the memo-hit and the fresh path. A control must exercise the MEMO-WARM path specifically, not only the cold one.
THE_MEMO_TRAP_IS_INHERITED.control: N-AO-7 (memo-warm refusal) and M-AO-6 (the mutation that moves the check to the fresh branch must turn a control RED).

translations.rule: Each translation resolves to the REFUSING value of a branch the boundary already has. No new refusal vocabulary is introduced.

points.why_routing_only: Every protected effect behind it transits K6 anyway. Without K3 the subject would still be refused, but by a throw instead of a coherent redirect.

points.why_required: Packet B measured that this boundary RETURNS an OrganizationContext which app/app/layout.tsx renders directly - tenant data reaching the response without further database-context transit. The same reasoning makes it required for L0.

Packet B measured consumers that take the context and query the raw db client scoping by ctx.organization.id, without transiting withOrganizationDatabaseContext - for those callers this null check IS the authorization decision.
points.inherits_the_null_discrimination_cost: Packet B NULL_DISCRIMINATION_ADJUDICATION_R4 accepted that an unverified subject becomes indistinguishable at C5 from a member with no selected organization. L0 ADDS A THIRD indistinguishable state - a verified subject who has not accepted. See OPEN_FINDINGS.F-AO-11.

points.vocabulary: throw with a new code, mapped to 403 - never 401
points.why_required: It is the convergence point for withAuthenticatedDatabaseContext (:688), withOrganizationDatabaseContext, withSuperAdminDatabaseContext and listSelectableMemberships. It is what makes the founding action and the invitation acceptance unreachable without editing either file.

points.disposition: NOT a release gate. NO control may depend on it. Packet B R4 proved all eleven of its call sites are preempted by C4 or C5, and reclassified it out of the completeness set. That reclassification is CONSUMED here, not re-litigated.

translations.http_semantics: The 401-at-C5 / 403-at-C6 adjudication frozen by Packet B HTTP_SEMANTICS_ADJUDICATION_R4 (Option A) is CONSUMED UNCHANGED. L0 introduces no new HTTP mapping. In particular K4 MUST remain a redirect and MUST NOT become a 401 - Packet B measured that a 401 or /login redirect there would loop via lib/supabase/proxy.ts:91.

explicitly_not_gated_by_L0.syncUserProfile: lib/auth/session.ts:371-412. Packet B PRE_VERIFICATION_WRITE_EXCEPTION freezes it as the sole pre-verification write. It is a fortiori pre-acceptance too: it writes the public.users row a principal needs to exist at all, so gating it on a state that only exists after that row would be circular.
explicitly_not_gated_by_L0.getCurrentUser_and_getCurrentMembership: lib/auth/session.ts:101 and :121. They grant nothing on their own and every downstream effect transits K4, K5 or K6. Gating them is the duplication the shape exists to avoid.
explicitly_not_gated_by_L0.the_acceptance_destination_itself: The route where L0 is discharged MUST be reachable by a subject who fails L0, or the gate is a lockout rather than a gate. It must therefore sit outside every one of K3..K7 - the same structural requirement Packet B B2 imposes on /verify-email.
explicitly_not_gated_by_L0.the_instrument_presentation_pages: app/(public)/terms, /terminos, /privacy, /privacidad must remain publicly reachable and ungated. A subject cannot be asked to accept a document they are refused permission to read.

L1_ATTACHMENT.status: SHAPE ONLY, and deliberately thinner than L0.
L1_ATTACHMENT.derivation_point: L1 predicate names an organization, so it is derived where an organization context is resolved - the K4/K5 region and withOrganizationDatabaseContext - never on the bare principal path. Deriving it at :536 would require reading acceptance state for an organization that is not yet in scope.
L1_ATTACHMENT.why_this_artifact_does_not_fix_L1_call_s: The set of boundaries where an organization context becomes an effect is the surface Packet A and the CommercialAccount/Entitlement lineage are both still moving. Pinning L1 call sites now would pin them against a topology that is scheduled to change, and the pins would be stale before implementation opens. What IS binding is the placement relative to the other gates and the fail-closed direction.
binding_properties: L1 is evaluated ONLY when an organization is in request scope. No organization in scope means L1 is NOT EVALUATED - it does not default to pass and it does not default to fail; the question is not asked. The no-scope case is answered by Packet A R2/R3 unchanged.

L1 refusal MUST NOT clear, write or otherwise mutate the selected-organization carrier. Packet A NO_CARRIER_WRITE_DURING_ROUTING keeps its sole permitted writer at app/(authenticated)/app/organizations/select/actions.ts, and L1 adds no exception.

L1 refusal MUST NOT fall back to another membership. Packet A R3.fallback_prohibition applies with equal force: an organization that has not accepted is not a reason to silently scope the subject to a different one.
L1 refusal MUST NOT enumerate memberships.

L1 is a PRECONDITION of entitlement evaluation, never itself an entitlement, and never itself an authorization. Ratification CA-03 - EntitlementGrant is distinct from authorization - and CA-05 - payment state does not directly grant authorization - are both preserved: acceptance state is a third thing that gates entitlement and grants nothing.
L1_ATTACHMENT.the_ordering_within_step_4_and_5: L1 precedes ENT. An organization that has not accepted must not have its entitlements evaluated, because an evaluated entitlement is the thing the journey places after acceptance. Evaluating and then discarding would leak the shape of the entitlement to a caller who has not passed the gate.

TERMINATION.requirement: The combined routing graph must terminate. No destination of B0, L0, R1..R5 or L1 may re-enter the chain with the same principal state.

the_new_hazard_this_artifact_introduces.measured_basis: Packet B B2.behaviour_at_the_destination specifies that /verify-email, for an AUTHENTICATED and VERIFIED subject, redirects to /app/dashboard, and its termination argument is that /app/dashboard passes B0 for a verified subject.
the_new_hazard_this_artifact_introduces.the_hazard: Once L0 exists, /app/dashboard no longer necessarily passes. A verified-but-unaccepted subject landing on /verify-email is redirected to /app/dashboard, where K4 refuses and redirects to the acceptance destination. That is a BOUNCE - it terminates, but through an extra hop - and Packet B B5 termination proof, which reasons about a two-state graph, no longer covers the three-state one.
the_new_hazard_this_artifact_introduces.ruling: The bounce TERMINATES and is therefore not a loop, but Packet B termination proof must be RE-STATED over the extended state space rather than assumed to carry. The implementing mission MUST re-derive it, and a control must assert termination over the extended graph.
the_new_hazard_this_artifact_introduces.the_cleaner_alternative_recorded_not_man: Packet B verified-subject redirect could target the next unsatisfied gate rather than /app/dashboard unconditionally. ATOMICITY_BOUNDARIES.rule: Each boundary below is ONE transaction. A boundary is complete or it did not happen. Boundaries are NEVER merged and NEVER split, and no boundary spans a network call or a redirect.

boundaries.name: ACCOUNT_LEGAL_ACCEPTANCE
contents: one account-class acceptance row per instrument accepted in this act

Granting an entitlement in the acceptance transaction would make acceptance an entitlement source and would contradict ratification CA-03. Entitlement evaluation is a separate act by the entitlement lineage.

contents: invitations status transition to accepted with accepted_at

boundaries.name: INVITATION_TERMINAL_STATE_TRANSITION
boundaries.status: SEPARATE BOUNDARY BY NECESSITY - this is the correction of F-AO-01.
boundaries.why_it_cannot_share_AB_4_transaction: The transition is followed by a REFUSAL. If the write and the refusal share a transaction, the refusal rolls the write back and the state never persists - which is exactly what is measured today at lib/invitations/service.ts:175-179. The durable-write-then-refuse pattern requires the write to COMMIT before the refusal is raised, or to be raised by a path that does not roll it back.
boundaries.requirement: The expired transition must be DURABLE across the refusal. Either it commits in its own transaction before the refusal, or the refusal is returned as a value rather than thrown inside the transaction.
boundaries.explicitly_not_prescribed: Which of those two shapes is used. Both satisfy durability. Prescribing one would be an implementation choice.

ATOMICITY_BOUNDARIES.CROSS_BOUNDARY_RULE: No boundary depends on another having succeeded within the same request. AB-1 commits and the subject continues; AB-2 commits and the subject continues; AB-3 commits and the subject continues. A failure in one leaves the journey resumable at that step and never leaves a half-built subject.

INVITATIONS.governing_decision: HPO-A.7 / HPO-A statement — invitation acceptance is a MUTATION and must occur via a PROPER MUTATING VERB (POST, or another proper mutating verb), never as a side effect of a render-time GET. See MUTATING_VERB_NORMATIVE_RULE for the binding formulation.

THE_DEFECT_AS_MEASURED.code_shape: A Server Component with no form and no action calls await withAuthenticatedDatabaseContext(() => acceptInvitation(token)) during the render of a GET request.
why_it_is_a_defect_and_not_merely_unfash: A GET is defined as safe. Anything that fetches the URL performs the mutation: a link preview crawler, an email client prefetch, a browser prerender, a security scanner, an antivirus URL check, a chat application unfurl. The membership can be created by software the invited person never used.

It is not idempotent in its OBSERVABLE effect even though the second call refuses: the first fetch consumes the invitation, so when the human finally clicks, they meet the refusal Invitation is no longer valid at lib/invitations/service.ts:172 - measured - and the journey is dead with no recovery path in the UI.

There is no user act to bind. HPO-A decision 4 requires acceptance evidence to record a subject affirmative act. A render triggered by a prefetch is not an act by the subject, and the audit row written at :210-217 would attribute it to them regardless.
The failure path mutates too: the expiry write at :175-178 fires on a render.
THE_DEFECT_AS_MEASURED.the_second_order_finding: F-AO-01 - even that expiry write does not persist, because the throw at :179 rolls back the transaction the caller opened. So the current design mutates on GET AND loses the one state transition it attempts. Both are corrected together or neither is.

MUTATING_VERB_NORMATIVE_RULE.status: BINDING. This is the live normative statement of the requirement. It replaces every POST-exclusive formulation in this artifact.
MUTATING_VERB_NORMATIVE_RULE.rule: Invitation acceptance is a MUTATION and MUST occur via a PROPER MUTATING VERB. It MUST NOT occur as a side effect of a render-time GET, or of any other safe method.
MUTATING_VERB_NORMATIVE_RULE.canonical_basis: HPO-A statement: Invitation acceptance is a mutation and must occur via POST (or another proper mutating verb), never as a side effect of a render-time GET request. Clause HPO-A.7 states the POST form; the statement carries the parenthetical, and the parenthetical is part of the ratification.
MUTATING_VERB_NORMATIVE_RULE.POST_is_the_expected_instance_not_the_ru: POST is the verb an implementation will normally choose and is fully conformant. So is PUT or DELETE where that verb is the semantically correct one for the operation. An implementation MUST NOT be rejected by this authority for choosing a proper mutating verb other than POST.
what_is_load_bearing: The request that causes the mutation declares a mutating method.
A safe-method request — GET or HEAD — performs NO mutation, on any path, including the expired and revoked refusal paths.
The mutation is caused by the subject affirmative act, not by a render.
MUTATING_VERB_NORMATIVE_RULE.R3_MATERIALIZATION_NOTE: R2 stated this correction as prose in INVITATIONS.R2_CORRECTION_MUTATING_VERB but left POST-exclusive wording standing in the normative text itself — in INVITATIONS.governing_decision, in INVITATIONS.REQUIRED_SHAPE, and in CANONICAL_JOURNEY.JOURNEY_INVITED_MEMBER. A supersession note beside a normative clause does not change the clause. R3 rewrites those sites so the live normative representation no longer implies POST-only. The R2 correction section is retained as the audit trail of why.

R1_the_link_target_is_a_RENDER_ONLY_page.requirement: The URL in an invitation email resolves to a page that READS and RENDERS and performs NO mutation of any kind. It displays what the subject is being invited to and presents an explicit affirmative control.
R1_the_link_target_is_a_RENDER_ONLY_page.prohibition: That page MUST NOT write any row, MUST NOT transition invitation status - including to expired - and MUST NOT create any membership.
R1_the_link_target_is_a_RENDER_ONLY_page.control: N-AO-8 asserts that a GET of the invitation URL leaves every table byte-identical.

R2_the_mutation_uses_a_proper_mutating_v.requirement: Membership creation happens only in response to an explicit request that DECLARES A MUTATING METHOD and originates from the subject affirmative act. POST is the expected instance and is fully conformant; PUT or DELETE is equally conformant where that verb is the semantically correct one. What is forbidden is causing the mutation from a safe method — a GET or HEAD render.
R2_the_mutation_uses_a_proper_mutating_v.boundary: AB-4, OWNED BY THE HANDLER, not inherited from a wrapper - see ATOMICITY_BOUNDARIES.AB-4.requirement.
R2_the_mutation_uses_a_proper_mutating_v.R3_RENAME_NOTE: This key was named R2_the_mutation_is_a_POST through R2 and its requirement text pinned POST exclusively. RENAMED and REWRITTEN at R3 so the live normative representation no longer implies POST-only. The correction was stated in prose at R2 (INVITATIONS.R2_CORRECTION_MUTATING_VERB) but the normative clause itself still said POST — a supersession note beside a clause does not change the clause. Authority: HPO-A statement parenthetical, MUTATING_VERB_NORMATIVE_RULE, F-AO-20.

R3_the_terminal_transitions_must_be_dura.requirement: Expiry and revocation state transitions must survive the refusal that accompanies them. See AB-5.
R3_the_terminal_transitions_must_be_dura.why_it_is_listed_as_a_separate_requireme: The conversion to a mutating verb does NOT fix this by itself. The same write-then-throw inside the same transaction fails identically under any verb. An implementation that converts the verb and declares HPO-A.7 discharged will ship the durability bug intact.

R4_ordering_against_the_gates.requirement: Invitation acceptance sits at step 4 of J-INVITED - after B0 and after L0. It is therefore behind K6 and unreachable for a subject who has not accepted the account instruments.
R4_ordering_against_the_gates.measured_basis: Packet B already proves that app/invite/accept/page.tsx:53 reaches its effect through withAuthenticatedDatabaseContext, which calls requirePrincipal at lib/auth/database-context.ts:688 - so C6, and therefore K6, preempts it WITHOUT editing the invitation file. The same property holds for the mutating-verb handler provided it also transits withAuthenticatedDatabaseContext.
R4_ordering_against_the_gates.the_trap_in_the_conversion: A mutating-verb handler that opens its own transaction directly, bypassing withAuthenticatedDatabaseContext in order to own its boundary per AB-4, would ALSO bypass requirePrincipal and therefore bypass both B0 and L0. Owning the transaction boundary and transiting the gate are two requirements and the conversion must satisfy both.
R4_ordering_against_the_gates.control: N-AO-10 asserts the mutating-verb handler refuses an unaccepted subject; M-AO-7 asserts that removing the gate transit from the handler turns it RED.

R5_redirect_target_preservation.requirement: The invitation target must be carried forward across B0 and L0 refusals so the subject resumes the invitation journey after satisfying them.
R5_redirect_target_preservation.measured_basis: The mechanism already exists: isSafeRedirectPath at app/(public)/login/actions.ts:22 and :78 and app/auth/callback/route.ts:10, and the invite page itself already builds /login?redirect=... at app/invite/accept/page.tsx:39. Packet B B4.invitation_target_preservation freezes the obligation for B0; L0 inherits it for the same reason.
R5_redirect_target_preservation.prohibition: The carried value must remain subject to the existing safe-path validation. A gate that carries an unvalidated target forward is an open redirect.

WHAT_INVITATION_ACCEPTANCE_IS_NOT.not_a_legal_acceptance: See ADJUDICATION_FOUNDER_VS_INVITED.A4. db/schema.ts:148 invitations.acceptedAt is a membership-lifecycle timestamp and is not acceptance evidence.
WHAT_INVITATION_ACCEPTANCE_IS_NOT.not_a_commercial_acceptance: Joining an organization does not accept its commercial instrument. Only an organization_admin discharges L1, once per organization.
WHAT_INVITATION_ACCEPTANCE_IS_NOT.not_an_identity_proof: The email equality check at lib/invitations/service.ts:181-183 confirms the invitation was ADDRESSED to this account. It does not prove the subject controls that address - that is B0 - and it must not be repurposed as a verification substitute.

ROLE_FALLBACK_NOTE.measured: lib/invitations/service.ts:190 falls back to ROLES.VIEWER when the stored invitation role fails isValidRole.

R2_CORRECTION_MUTATING_VERB.status: BINDING CORRECTION of an R1 over-narrowing.
R2_CORRECTION_MUTATING_VERB.what_R1_said: Invitation acceptance must mutate by POST, never render-time GET — with POST pinned exclusively throughout REQUIRED_SHAPE.R2 and the surrounding clauses.
R2_CORRECTION_MUTATING_VERB.what_canonical_says: HPO-A statement: Invitation acceptance is a mutation and must occur via POST (or another proper mutating verb), never as a side effect of a render-time GET request. Clause HPO-A.7 states the POST form; the statement carries the parenthetical.
R2_CORRECTION_MUTATING_VERB.THE_CORRECTED_REQUIREMENT: Invitation acceptance MUST occur via a PROPER MUTATING VERB — POST being the expected instance — and MUST NOT occur as a side effect of a render-time GET. An implementation using PUT or DELETE where that is the semantically correct verb SATISFIES this requirement and MUST NOT be refused on the basis of this artifact.
R2_CORRECTION_MUTATING_VERB.what_is_load_bearing_and_what_is_not: Load-bearing: the request must be a mutation by its own declared semantics, and a GET render must not mutate. NOT load-bearing: the literal string POST. R1 conflated the instance with the rule.
what_does_NOT_change: The measured defect is unchanged. app/invite/accept/page.tsx:53 calls acceptInvitation during the render of a GET, and that violates the requirement under either phrasing.
F-AO-01 is unchanged and is not a verb question at all. The expiry write at lib/invitations/service.ts:175-178 is rolled back by the throw at :179 regardless of which verb reaches it. AB-5 stands.
R4 of REQUIRED_SHAPE is unchanged: the handler must transit the gate AND own its transaction boundary, and satisfying one by breaking the other is the trap M-AO-7 exists to catch.
R1 of REQUIRED_SHAPE is unchanged and is the half that actually carries the safety property: the link target renders and mutates nothing, asserted by N-AO-8 over a byte-identical snapshot.
R2_CORRECTION_MUTATING_VERB.manifest_consequence: The companion manifest control is re-scoped to assert the PROPERTY — a safe-method request performs no mutation, and the mutating request declares a mutating method — rather than asserting the literal verb POST. See N-AO-33.

MULTI_ORG.status: BINDING AS A CONSTRAINT ON THE FUTURE IMPLEMENTATION. No removal is authorized here.
MULTI_ORG.governing_decision: HPO-A decision 8 - the physical single-active-membership constraint incompatible with multi-org must be removed in the future implementation.

WHAT_DECISION_8_TARGETS.the_object: db/schema.ts:112 uniqueIndex('user_single_active_membership').on(table.userId).where(status = 'active'). Materialized in db/baseline/stella_g2_schema.sql and db/migrations/0003_curvy_tempest.sql.
WHAT_DECISION_8_TARGETS.why_it_is_incompatible: Ratification MO-02 states that a subject may hold ACTIVE memberships in MULTIPLE organizations. A partial unique index on user_id where status = active permits exactly one. The contradiction is structural, not interpretive.

REMOVAL_IS_NOT_A_DROP_INDEX.status: THE CENTRAL FINDING OF THIS SECTION.
REMOVAL_IS_NOT_A_DROP_INDEX.F_AO_03_restated: db/prepared/stella_0006_invitation_capability.sql:165 and db/prepared/stella_0010_organization_bootstrap_capability.sql:140 each test for the index existence as a PRECONDITION, and each RAISES at :169 and :144 respectively with the message: requires the PARTIAL UNIQUE index user_single_active_membership on organization_members; it is the only thing that serialises two concurrent acceptances or bootstraps that use different keys.
REMOVAL_IS_NOT_A_DROP_INDEX.consequence_1_the_capabilities_refuse: Dropping the index does not degrade those two prepared units. It makes them REFUSE TO APPLY, by their own explicit precondition. Any lineage that drops the index without re-authoring both units breaks the apply path.
REMOVAL_IS_NOT_A_DROP_INDEX.consequence_2_a_concurrency_control_is_r: By those units own words the index is the ONLY serialisation for two concurrent acceptances or bootstraps under differing idempotency keys. Removing it removes a CONCURRENCY CONTROL, not merely a cardinality ceiling. A replacement must land first or together.
REMOVAL_IS_NOT_A_DROP_INDEX.the_replacement_shape_already_exists_in_: db/prepared/stella_0010_organization_bootstrap_capability.sql:198-216 declares an idempotency ledger with PRIMARY KEY (user_id, idempotency_key), and :216 explains that the function claims the key by INSERT before any other write so the primary key serialises concurrent calls. COMMERCIAL_ACCOUNT_ENTITLEMENT_AUTHORITY cap05_reconciliation.properties_to_preserve names that same ledger first. This artifact does NOT design the replacement and does not assert the ledger is sufficient - it records that the shape is already present and that the successor is obliged to preserve it.
REMOVAL_IS_NOT_A_DROP_INDEX.F_AO_02_restated: There is a SECOND ceiling in application code: lib/invitations/service.ts:185-187 queries getCurrentMembership and throws You already belong to an organization. It does not consult the index. Dropping the index alone leaves invitation acceptance refusing at :186, before reaching any INSERT.
therefore_decision_8_requires_all_of: A replacement serialisation mechanism for concurrent acceptance and bootstrap.
Re-authoring the two prepared capability preconditions, by their own authority - NOT by this artifact and NOT by whichever mission implements acceptance.
Removing or reshaping the application-level ceiling at lib/invitations/service.ts:185-187.

Re-verification of every consumer of the notion of THE single active membership - lib/auth/database-context.ts resolves the active organization as the caller active membership, which MO-03 records as pick-first rather than selected.
REMOVAL_IS_NOT_A_DROP_INDEX.measurement_caveat: The grep also returned 67 files under db/migrations/meta/ (0003_snapshot.json through 0069_snapshot.json). Those are drizzle-generated state, not hand-authored dependencies, and are NOT a work surface: they change as a consequence of a migration, never as an edit.

WHAT_DECISION_8_DOES_NOT_AUTHORIZE: It does not authorize this artifact, or any acceptance-implementing mission, to drop the index. The index belongs to the tenancy/multi-org lineage and its removal is that lineage allocation.

It does not relax founder cardinality. MO-01 - a subject may self-service-found at most ONE organization - is a DIFFERENT ceiling, enforced by a DIFFERENT object: organizations_self_service_founder_unique at db/schema.ts:89-91. Decision 8 targets MEMBERSHIP cardinality and leaves FOUNDING cardinality untouched. MO-02 states the distinction directly: self-service founding cardinality and membership cardinality are different concepts. Conflating them would remove a control HPO-A never mentioned.

It does not create a selected-organization mechanism. MO-03 requires one and MO-03 own REQUIRED_RESOLUTION records that it cannot be built until MO-02 ceiling is addressed. Decision 8 unblocks that work; it does not perform it.
It does not authorize a CommercialAccount governing several organizations to widen tenant scope. MULTIORG_INTERSECTION.hard_separation is preserved.

WHAT_MULTI_ORG_MEANS_FOR_THE_ACCEPTANCE_.account_class_is_unaffected: L0 is per-subject and asks no tenancy question. A subject with memberships in five organizations accepts Terms and Privacy exactly once, and reaccepts exactly once when required. Membership cardinality has no effect on L0 whatsoever - which is a direct benefit of placing L0 before the tenancy question.
WHAT_MULTI_ORG_MEANS_FOR_THE_ACCEPTANCE_.organization_class_is_per_organization: L1 is evaluated against the organization in request scope. A subject who is organization_admin of two organizations may face L1 in one and not the other, and discharging it in one does NOT discharge it in the other. Grounds: HPO-A decision 2 makes the acceptance organization-level; there is no account-level or CommercialAccount-level shortcut.
WHAT_MULTI_ORG_MEANS_FOR_THE_ACCEPTANCE_.the_CommercialAccount_trap: One CommercialAccount may govern several organizations (CA-02, and the FK carrier exists at db/schema.ts:83). It is tempting to record commercial acceptance once per CommercialAccount rather than once per organization. THAT IS FORBIDDEN: HPO-A decision 2 says organization-level, and CA-08 already establishes that CommercialAccount-level aggregation does NOT create implicit shared authorization or pooled runtime state. An acceptance recorded at CommercialAccount level would grant an organization that never accepted anything a passing L1 by inheritance.
WHAT_MULTI_ORG_MEANS_FOR_THE_ACCEPTANCE_.control: N-AO-12 asserts that discharging L1 for organization A leaves organization B refusing, including when both are governed by the same CommercialAccount.

A3_REMEDY_RESOLUTION.status: RESOLVED BY RAT-AO-01, PARTIALLY. The resolution is bounded and the boundary is stated.
A3_REMEDY_RESOLUTION.what_R1_left_open: R1 ADJUDICATION_FOUNDER_VS_INVITED.A3 derived that a member of an organization with an undischarged L1 has no entitled product capability there, then recorded the REMEDY as STOP_FOR_HPO (F-AO-05): what the blocked member is told, and whether the administrator is notified.

WHAT_IS_NOW_RESOLVED.the_blocked_non_admin: Receives a NON-SENSITIVE BLOCKED STATE — enough to explain that access is pending, and no more. They cannot satisfy the obligation and cannot bypass it. RAT-AO-01 AO1_C2 and AO1_C3.
WHAT_IS_NOW_RESOLVED.the_authorized_organization_admin: Receives the COMPLETION CALL-TO-ACTION on an appropriate governed surface — the affordance that lets the obligation actually be satisfied. RAT-AO-01 AO1_C4.

WHAT_REMAINS_UNRATIFIED.automatic_notification: NOT RATIFIED AND NOT INVENTED. Canonical RAT-AO-01 says the organization_admin RECEIVES the completion CTA. Receiving an affordance on a surface you visit is not the same as being sent a message. Whether any email, in-app notification, digest or webhook fires is OUTSIDE this ratification.
WHAT_REMAINS_UNRATIFIED.the_specific_prohibition: This artifact MUST NOT infer, require, design or assert an automatic notification side effect, and no control in the companion manifest may depend on one. See SECURITY_PROHIBITIONS.X-AO-14.

THE_RECONCILIATION.RAT_OP_01_verbatim_relevant_half: Commercial V1 permits issuance of a SUPPORT_CAPABILITY only to a natural person who holds an ACTIVE membership in the affected organization with role EXACTLY organization_admin. hasRole('>=') / role-hierarchy / '+' notation and implicit admission of tenant super_admin are all excluded. Tenant super_admin is not automatically an authorizer.
THE_RECONCILIATION.RAT_AO_02_relevant_half: No platform-admin, support or commercial-team actor may record an organization application legal or commercial acceptance on that organization behalf. Acceptance is performed only by an active organization_admin.
THE_RECONCILIATION.they_are_consistent_and_mutually_reinfor: Both require an ACTIVE membership with role EXACTLY organization_admin, both explicitly exclude a hierarchy threshold, and both explicitly exclude implicit admission of tenant super_admin. RAT-OP-01 constrains who may AUTHORIZE a support capability; RAT-AO-02 constrains who may PERFORM an acceptance. Different acts, identical predicate shape.
THE_RECONCILIATION.the_derived_corollary: SUPPORT CAPABILITY DOES NOT CONFER ACCEPTANCE AUTHORITY. A platform principal that has been issued a support capability under RAT-OP-01 has thereby acquired a support capability and nothing else. Acceptance authority is not among the things a support capability can carry, because RAT-AO-02 AO2_C2 restricts the act to an active organization_admin of the affected organization, and a platform principal holding a support capability is not thereby an active organization_admin.
THE_RECONCILIATION.DERIVED_NOT_GRANTED: The corollary is a DERIVATION from the conjunction of the two ratifications. Neither states it in those words. It is labelled so that an auditor can challenge the derivation rather than mistake it for ratified text — though note that RAT-OP-01 explicit_non_authorizations independently says it does not grant standing tenant-content access, which points the same way.
THE_RECONCILIATION.no_platform_bypass: There is NO platform path — support capability, super-admin bit, tenant super_admin role value, impersonation, or operator tooling — that records or satisfies L0 or L1. L0 is writable only by the subject for themselves; L1 only by an active organization_admin of the affected organization.

FAIL_CLOSED.global_rule: Where acceptance state is UNKNOWN, UNREADABLE or AMBIGUOUS, the gate REFUSES. An unreadable acceptance relation is a refusal, never a pass. This is the ODS fail-closed rule applied to this domain: where authority is UNKNOWN or ambiguous, preserve or stop - never guess.

FC_1_ACCEPTANCE_MISSING.case: A required instrument has never been accepted by the subject (L0) or for the organization (L1).
FC_1_ACCEPTANCE_MISSING.behaviour: REFUSE. Translate at the boundary into the vocabulary it already speaks - redirect at K3/K4, null at K5, throw mapped to 403 at K6.
FC_1_ACCEPTANCE_MISSING.destination: The acceptance destination for the failing class. For L0, a route reachable by a subject who fails L0 and outside every enforcement point. For L1, a route reachable by an organization_admin of the scoped organization.
PROHIBITED_SIDE_EFFECTS_OF_THE_REFUSAL: MUST NOT auto-select an organization. Packet A NO_AUTO_SELECTION remains BINDING and this artifact adds no exception to it.
MUST NOT write, clear or otherwise mutate the selected-organization carrier. The sole permitted writer remains app/(authenticated)/app/organizations/select/actions.ts.
MUST NOT enumerate memberships. Enumeration discloses tenancy shape to a subject who has not met a precondition.
MUST NOT create, infer, backdate or default an acceptance row. There is no implied acceptance, no acceptance-by-continued-use, and no acceptance-by-dismissing-a-banner.
MUST NOT grant, evaluate or partially evaluate any entitlement.
MUST NOT emit an audit row. A refusal is a routing decision; auditing every blocked page view would flood audit_logs with non-events. The ACCEPTANCE is audited; the refusal is not.
FC_1_ACCEPTANCE_MISSING.the_refusal_is_stateless: Nothing about the subject or organization changes because they were refused. The same request repeated produces the same refusal, and satisfying the gate produces a pass with no cleanup required.

FC_2_VERSION_SUPERSEDED_WITH_REACCEPT_RE.case: A later version of an already-accepted instrument is published and marked reaccept_required.
FC_2_VERSION_SUPERSEDED_WITH_REACCEPT_RE.behaviour: IDENTICAL TO FC-1. The subject or organization is non-current and is refused at the same gate, in the same position, with the same vocabulary.
FC_2_VERSION_SUPERSEDED_WITH_REACCEPT_RE.grounds: REACCEPTANCE.THE_REACCEPTANCE_JOURNEY_POSITION - decision 5 changes when the predicate goes false, not how many gates exist.
FC_2_VERSION_SUPERSEDED_WITH_REACCEPT_RE.the_prior_acceptance_is_UNTOUCHED: No UPDATE, no DELETE, no is_current flip. The prior row remains as evidence of what was accepted and when. Currency is recomputed, never rewritten.
FC_2_VERSION_SUPERSEDED_WITH_REACCEPT_RE.no_grace_period: NOT AUTHORIZED. HPO-A grants none, and a grace period is by definition a window in which the gate is open. See OPEN_FINDINGS.F-AO-08.
FC_2_VERSION_SUPERSEDED_WITH_REACCEPT_RE.the_asymmetry_that_must_be_preserved: A later version published WITHOUT reaccept_required does NOT refuse. The subject stays current on their older version. An implementation that refuses on any version change has implemented the naive predicate REACCEPTANCE forbids, and the failure is a false lockout of the entire user base.
controls: P-AO-6 - later unmarked version leaves the subject passing
N-AO-4 - later marked version turns the subject refusing
M-AO-3 - replacing the predicate with latest-version equality must turn P-AO-6 RED

FC_3_BOOTSTRAP_PARTIALLY_FAILS.behaviour: THE WHOLE TRANSACTION ROLLS BACK. There is no state in which an organization exists without its CommercialAccount, its founding membership, its initial entitlement state, or its audit rows.
FC_3_BOOTSTRAP_PARTIALLY_FAILS.grounds: HPO-A decision 6, and COMMERCIAL_ACCOUNT_ENTITLEMENT_AUTHORITY SELF_SERVICE.frozen which already states there is no state in which an Organization exists without its CommercialAccount or its founding membership.
FC_3_BOOTSTRAP_PARTIALLY_FAILS.WHAT_MUST_NOT_BE_ROLLED_BACK: AB-1. The subject account acceptance happened EARLIER, in its own committed transaction, and is evidence of a past act. A failed bootstrap does not un-accept the Terms. An implementation that wraps L0 and AB-2 in one transaction to simplify the flow destroys evidence on an unrelated failure.
FC_3_BOOTSTRAP_PARTIALLY_FAILS.IDEMPOTENT_RETRY: The retry claims the SAME idempotency key and either recognises the prior successful attempt or proceeds. It must NEVER produce a second organization. Measured gap: the LIVE path has no idempotency key at all - CAP-05 section 1.2 - so today a resubmitted POST after a timeout creates a second organization or collides on slug.

THE_STATE_THAT_IS_NOT_A_PARTIAL_FAILURE.state: ORGANIZATION_PENDING_COMMERCIAL_ACCEPTANCE - AB-2 committed, AB-3 has not happened.
THE_STATE_THAT_IS_NOT_A_PARTIAL_FAILURE.ruling: This is a SUCCESSFUL bootstrap, not a partial one. It MUST NOT be rolled back, cleaned up, garbage-collected, or reported as an incomplete organization.
THE_STATE_THAT_IS_NOT_A_PARTIAL_FAILURE.why_this_needs_saying: An operator or a cleanup job looking for organizations without commercial acceptance would find every freshly founded organization and could delete real customer data. The window is intended - see CANONICAL_JOURNEY.THE_WINDOW_THIS_CREATES.
THE_STATE_THAT_IS_NOT_A_PARTIAL_FAILURE.control: N-AO-11 asserts that an organization in this state is intact and its founder can still discharge L1.

FC_4_INVITATION_EXPIRED_OR_REVOKED.case: The invitation status is not pending, or expiresAt is in the past.
FC_4_INVITATION_EXPIRED_OR_REVOKED.measured_today: lib/invitations/service.ts:171-173 throws for a non-pending status; :174-180 marks expired and throws for a past expiresAt.
REQUIRED_CORRECTIONS: The refusal must not be reachable by a GET render - decision 7, and R1 of the required shape.
The expired transition must be DURABLE across the refusal - AB-5, correcting F-AO-01. Today it is rolled back by the throw at :179.
FC_4_INVITATION_EXPIRED_OR_REVOKED.revoked_case_note: Revocation is covered by the non-pending branch at :171-173 and requires no state transition on the accept path, so it does not carry F-AO-01. It is listed separately because the two cases share a refusal but not a write.
FC_4_INVITATION_EXPIRED_OR_REVOKED.no_partial_acceptance: A refused invitation leaves NO organization_members row, NO invitation status change other than the durable terminal transition, and NO audit row claiming acceptance.
FC_4_INVITATION_EXPIRED_OR_REVOKED.the_ordering_note: The invitation refusal is evaluated INSIDE AB-4, after B0 and L0 have already passed at K6. An expired invitation held by an unaccepted subject is refused by L0 FIRST, not by the expiry check - the subject never learns the invitation state until they have accepted the account instruments. That is the correct order and it is a deliberate consequence of the gate chain, not an oversight.
controls: N-AO-9 - expired status observable after refusal

FC_5_NO_ORGANIZATION_SELECTED.case: The subject has passed B0 and L0 but no organization is in request scope.
FC_5_NO_ORGANIZATION_SELECTED.behaviour: ANSWERED BY PACKET A, UNCHANGED. L1 IS NOT EVALUATED.
FC_5_NO_ORGANIZATION_SELECTED.grounds: L1 predicate names an organization. With no organization in scope the predicate has no argument, so the question is not asked. L1 does NOT default to pass and does NOT default to fail - it is undefined and therefore skipped, and the routing decision belongs to Packet A R2 or R3.
packet_a_behaviour_preserved_verbatim: R2 - membership null and refusal code TENANCY_NO_ORGANIZATION_SELECTED: enumerate via listSelectableMemberships(); zero candidates route to /app/onboarding; one or more route to /app/organizations/select, INCLUDING exactly one.
R3 - membership null and refusal code TENANCY_SELECTED_ORGANIZATION_NOT_A_MEMBER: clear the stale carrier THEN redirect to the selector, in that order.
R4 - RETURN SITE 3, where membership is non-null and the code is reused for an unreadable organization row, is matched by NEITHER R2 NOR R3 and remains excluded.
NO_AUTO_SELECTION - the single-candidate case gets no shortcut.
FC_5_NO_ORGANIZATION_SELECTED.THE_TRAP_THIS_CASE_EXISTS_TO_FORBID: An implementer who reads the journey as a linear pipeline may make L1 refuse when there is no organization, reasoning that no organization means no acceptance. That would refuse every subject at the selector - the very place they go to acquire a scope - and would produce a lockout indistinguishable from a loop. L1 must be SKIPPED, not failed, when no organization is in scope.
controls: P-AO-8 - a subject with no scope reaches the Packet A destination unchanged
N-AO-13 - L1 is not evaluated with no scope, asserted by the absence of any acceptance query on that path
M-AO-8 - making L1 refuse on a null scope must turn P-AO-8 RED

FC_6_ACCEPTANCE_STATE_UNREADABLE.case: The acceptance or version relation cannot be read - RLS refusal, missing relation, query error.
FC_6_ACCEPTANCE_STATE_UNREADABLE.behaviour: REFUSE. An unreadable gate is a closed gate.
FC_6_ACCEPTANCE_STATE_UNREADABLE.grounds: The CLAUDE.md fail-closed rule, and the same posture the repository already takes at db/identity-context.ts, where a rejected identity never reaches a commit.
FC_6_ACCEPTANCE_STATE_UNREADABLE.explicit_prohibition: MUST NOT be caught and converted into a pass. MUST NOT be logged-and-continued. A try/catch around the currency query whose catch branch returns true is the single most likely way this entire model is defeated, and it would be invisible in every positive test.
FC_6_ACCEPTANCE_STATE_UNREADABLE.control: M-AO-5 - replacing the currency query failure path with a permissive default must turn a negative control RED.

FC_7_NO_INSTRUMENT_PUBLISHED.case: The registry contains no published applicable version for a REQUIRED instrument — the state at first deployment, and any later state in which a required instrument has no version in effect.
FC_7_NO_INSTRUMENT_PUBLISHED.behaviour: REFUSE. FAIL CLOSED. This is now DERIVED, not an owner decision.
FC_7_NO_INSTRUMENT_PUBLISHED.R2_STOP_FOR_HPO_WITHDRAWN: R2 classified this STOP_FOR_HPO on the reasoning that a conjunction over an empty set is vacuously true, so the gate would pass, and that HPO-A does not choose between passing and refusing. That framing contained the error: it defined the conjunction over WHATEVER KEYS HAPPEN TO BE PUBLISHED, which makes the required set a function of the registry contents. Under that definition an empty registry genuinely is ambiguous — but the definition itself was wrong.

THE_CORRECTED_DEFINITION.the_conjunction_is_over_the_CLOSED_REQUI: Owner policy already fixes which instrument classes exist and their cardinality: HPO-A.1 requires account-level Terms AND Privacy acceptance before product access; HPO-A.2 and HPO-A.3 require an organization-level commercial acceptance. The REQUIRED set is fixed by ratification. It is NOT derived from what the registry happens to contain.
THE_CORRECTED_DEFINITION.consequence: The gate evaluates: for each instrument in the CLOSED REQUIRED SET, is the subject or organization current? A required instrument with no published applicable version cannot be current for anyone, so the conjunct is FALSE and the gate REFUSES. There is no empty set and therefore no vacuous truth.
THE_CORRECTED_DEFINITION.why_this_is_derivation_and_not_a_choice: Once the required set is recognised as ratified rather than registry-derived, only one answer is constructible. The vacuous-pass reading required treating the required set as empty, and HPO-A.1 forbids that: it states the acceptance is REQUIRED before product access, which is false of a platform that grants access with nothing published.

FC_7_NO_INSTRUMENT_PUBLISHED.the_operational_reading: A deployment with no published instruments cannot onboard anyone. That is the correct behaviour and it is detected immediately. It is an IMPLEMENTATION AND PUBLISHING DEPENDENCY — publish the required instruments — not an unresolved product question.
FC_7_NO_INSTRUMENT_PUBLISHED.what_remains_with_counsel: WHICH TEXT each required instrument carries, whether it is legally sufficient, and which locale is controlling. LRF-01 and LRF-02 are untouched by this reclassification. Counsel controls the CONTENT; the owner has already fixed the CLASSES and the cardinality; this artifact derives the gate behaviour.
FC_7_NO_INSTRUMENT_PUBLISHED.control: P-AO-15 is RETAINED and RE-SCOPED: it asserts refusal when a REQUIRED instrument has no published applicable version, which is now a derived requirement rather than an interim posture pending an owner decision.

R2_BLOCK_SUPERSEDED.case: The registry contains no published instrument for a class - the state at first deployment, before any instrument exists.
R2_BLOCK_SUPERSEDED.behaviour: STOP_FOR_HPO. This artifact does NOT decide it.
the_two_readings: Vacuous pass - a conjunction over an empty set is true, so L0 passes and the journey proceeds. This is mathematically natural and operationally convenient, and it means a deployment that forgot to publish its instruments silently has no gate.
Refuse - no instrument means the platform is not ready to onboard anyone, consistent with LC0 gating self_service_onboarding on the ABSENCE of acceptance capability.
R2_BLOCK_SUPERSEDED.why_this_is_not_derivable: The first reading follows from the logic of the predicate. The second follows from the purpose of the gate. HPO-A does not choose, and the choice has a real operational consequence in exactly the situation where a mistake is most likely - initial deployment. Guessing here would be inventing owner policy on the highest-risk edge of the model.
R2_BLOCK_SUPERSEDED.INTERIM_POSTURE_UNTIL_ADJUDICATED: REFUSE, and make the refusal loud. That is the fail-closed direction, it is reversible if the owner chooses vacuous pass, and its failure mode - nobody can onboard until instruments are published - is detected immediately, whereas the other reading fails silently and is detected by an auditor months later.

THE_CONTENT_LEAK_PROHIBITION.measured_hazard: Prior repository evidence records that audit_logs before_json and after_json carry VERBATIM content in many verbs.
THE_CONTENT_LEAK_PROHIBITION.ruling: An acceptance audit row MUST NOT carry instrument TEXT. It carries the instrument_key, the version, the content DIGEST, the subject or organization identifier, and the timestamp.
THE_CONTENT_LEAK_PROHIBITION.grounds: The digest already identifies the document uniquely, and the bytes are retained once in the instrument registry. Copying them into every acceptance audit row duplicates a potentially large document per acceptance for no evidentiary gain, and puts instrument text into a table read by operator surfaces.
THE_CONTENT_LEAK_PROHIBITION.the_reverse_risk_also_recorded: The audit row must not carry personal data beyond the subject identifier that the acceptance row does not already carry. In particular, if the owner later authorizes capturing an IP address on an acceptance (LRF-03), that value must not be duplicated into the audit payload without its own decision.

TENANT_SCOPE_OF_THE_AUDIT_ROW.account_class: An account-class acceptance is NOT tenant data - it belongs to a subject who may belong to no organization at all, and at the moment of L0 in J-FOUNDER they demonstrably do not. Its audit row therefore has NO organization scope.
TENANT_SCOPE_OF_THE_AUDIT_ROW.the_consequence_that_must_be_handled: The repository audit emitter is organization-oriented: the live founding action passes organizationId at app/(authenticated)/app/onboarding/actions.ts:146 and :156, and acceptInvitation passes invitation.organizationId at lib/invitations/service.ts:212 and :220. An account-class acceptance has no such value.
TENANT_SCOPE_OF_THE_AUDIT_ROW.measured_precedent: Packet B PRE_VERIFICATION_WRITE_EXCEPTION.WHAT_IT_MUST_NOT_BE_ABLE_TO_CREATE includes any audit row carrying tenant scope, which establishes that a pre-tenancy act must not fabricate one. The same applies to L0.
TENANT_SCOPE_OF_THE_AUDIT_ROW.requirement: The account-class acceptance audit row must be emitted with a genuinely absent organization scope, NOT with a fabricated, borrowed, or later-backfilled one.
TENANT_SCOPE_OF_THE_AUDIT_ROW.THE_EMITTER_ALREADY_ADMITS_THIS_SHAPE_ME: db/schema.ts:118 declares auditLogs.organizationId as uuid('organization_id').references(() => organizations.id) with NO .notNull() - it is NULLABLE. lib/audit/logger.ts:288 and :407 both declare organizationId?: string - OPTIONAL. So no emitter change is required and none is authorized. This corrects an inherited claim that only two verbs admit organization_id NULL: that claim is about which VERBS pass the value, not about whether the emitter and column admit its absence. The structural capability exists at this AS_OF_TREE.
TENANT_SCOPE_OF_THE_AUDIT_ROW.what_remains_an_obligation: The implementing mission must confirm that the RLS insert policy governing audit_logs admits a row with a NULL organization_id written by the acceptance path. Column nullability and emitter optionality are necessary but not sufficient - a policy could still refuse. NOT MEASURED by this lane, which ran no PostgreSQL probe.

AUDIT.organization_class_scope: An organization-class acceptance IS tenant data and its audit row carries the organization scope, exactly as the existing membership and invitation verbs do.
